messages.subject: Re: Empty tabix files from regionCounts
messages.body_plain:
Hi David,

The segfault error indicates we are running out of memory. The traceback shows that the function failed during the file-loading. But anyway, it worked (even though it errored) before with the tabix files.

Concerning the difference between CpG and CHH coverage, I think it greatly depends on the organism/tissue that you are studying. In mammals, cytosines CpG context are known to cluster in CpG-islands on promoter regions of the gene, while non-CpG cytosines occur on repetitive DNA sequences or transposable elements. So maybe your CHH sites are located in intergenic regions? You could check this with genomation (https://bioconductor.org/packages/devel/bioc/vignettes/methylKit/inst/doc/methylKit.html#4_Annotating_differentially_methylated_bases_or_regions)  or annotatr (https://bioconductor.org/packages/release/bioc/html/annotatr.html)

Best,
Alex

messages.subject: Re: assembly and annotation bed file
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

for any gff-based annotation prepared with gffToGRanges() please use `annotateWithFeatures()` instead of `annotateWithGeneParts()` for the final step.

annotateWithGeneParts() expects as features (second arg) a "GRangesList object containing GRanges object for promoter, exons, introns and transcription start sites, or simply output of readTranscriptFeatures function",
while annotateWithFeatures() just needs "a named GRangesList object containing GRanges objects different set of features".

To fix your code:

```
gene.obj = gffToGRanges("contigs.emapper.genepred.gff")
head(gene.obj)
split = as(split(gene.obj, gene.obj$type), "GRangesList")
head(split)

diffAnn=annotateWithFeatures(as(myDiffFiltered,"GRanges"), split)
```

Best,
Alex

messages.subject: are promoter region counts counted twice? and some additional minor questions
messages.subject_clean: are promoter region counts counted twice? and some additional minor questions
messages.body_plain:
Dear Methylkit Team and Community,

I am currently analysing mouse sperm methylation data, comparing a control vs offsprings. i am using bismark coverage file, thus i dont always know on which strand distinct C was found in the CpG context.
 DMR analysis with 1k or 1kk window and step size was straightforward and I also used the methylation percent data for a genome-wide violin plot with all filtered and normalized CpGs (NOT selected for the significantly different DMRs). Here my first question: since this data is by far not normally districuted and the number of datapoints is huge, simple statistical tests like t-test wont work to see if there is a significant difference between the sperm samples. What would you reccommend here for methylation data with percent methylation for each region as data point for each sperm sample (e.g. region1 : sperm 1-1/80%, sperm 1-2/70%, sperm 2-1/20%, sperm 2-2/0%, region2: ... etc)?

methylation_perc_ctr-vs-all_chr1-x-y_1mioWindow.png
 <https://1drv.ms/i/s!At_TeNxxLhDTljPbiOkgoHLpK0AL>

Thereafter, I thought it would be good to explore promoter regions. I used the standard setting of methylkit's
gene.obj <- readTranscriptFeatures("GRCm38.bed")  function so i have a 2k long promoter at the TSS anootated. here my next question: is it normal to have promoter regions so crammed together at some sites? in my snippet you see that at chr 19 the 61227462 and thereafter only 1 nt later already the start of my next promoter. should i be worried? this is a standard table browser bed-file output for the GRCm38 genome.

what i would want to do thereafter is:
meth <- unite(filtered.normalized.myobj) to have all counts together and then:
meth_promoter <- regionCounts(meth, gene.obj$promoters, cov.bases=5) so that i only sum the counts of CpGs that overlap with promoter regions. how does methylkit anyways deal with counts of unknow strand-origin? especially if genes or promoter regions seem to overlap (as shown in my second snippet above), will counts be counted twice then? this would confuse me more and i wouldn't know how to deal with that when doing statistical work later. in the third snippet this is visible as some start sites are sitting very close to each other and thus the region overlap and the counts between these two regions is then exactly the same (row 5 and 6 or 14 and 15).

 This time the methylation percentage distribution looks differently as seen in my third snippet. looks like promoter CpG methylation distribution is different compared to whole genome CpG distribution.

For the promoter methylation percentage i would also ask myself how to statistically best analyse such an output between groups. especially since promoter regions are somehow counted twice (or their methylation coverage).

lastly, should i use meth_promoter (after regionCounts()) from above to calculateDiffMeth(meth_promoter) and get the differentially methylated promoters (and gene names indirectly) OR should i at first carry out the normal DML pipeline from the beginning to get CpG sites that are differentially methylated, and then overlap with the promoters manually somehow?
For the first case, i could directly read out the bigges difference in methylation (with statistics) between promoter regions. In the second case, i would have the significant DML, selected for promoter regions, which i could use to calculate the average per promoter of methylation difference and then readout the respective gene name.

thank you for all your input. if i have a bug in my thought process please let me also know. thank you : )

best. tom

messages.subject: methylkit question
messages.body_plain:
My name is Nilanjana. I am analyzing Enzymatic Methylation sequencing data using methylKit package. My goal is to check how the methylation pattern differs in different genomic features (promoter, enhancer, and gene body region, and if possible also at CTCF binding regions). I have only one sample, from the DLBCL patient, and no control data. I have a list of genes that are found to be usually differentially methylated in DLBCL patients. Can I plot the average methylation signal of these gene coordinates over the specific genomic regions (such as promoter, gene body, and enhancer)?  And find out the genes that are hyper and hypo-methylated. Further, I want to look at the pathway enriched by these genes. I do not happen to find proper guidelines on how to do the analysis without a control. Any help would be greatly appreciated. Thank you.

Regards,
Nilanjana
